mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized signals inflationary pressures that may lead to monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL growth > 2% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP signals economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of periods following GDP growth, or GDP growth does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decline > 1% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a mismatch in labor market dynamics, leading to uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% signals increased borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > 2% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline > 1% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).
